title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench

body: In real-world software development, code review typically involves iterative interactions between developers and reviewers to improve software quality, making the process costly and time-consuming. Although recent work explores large language models (LLMs) for automated code review, most approaches oversimplify code review into a single-round, static decision task, which fails to capture the multi-round interactive nature and the complex problem-solving processes inherent in realistic review scenarios. To bridge this gap, we introduce MCR-Bench, the first defect state-aware benchmark designed for realistic multi-round code review. MCR-Bench covers five commonly-used programming languages and consists of 2,269 real-world multi-round code review tasks, each of which is annotated with fine-grained defect information and cross-round state labels. Each task in MCR-Bench is equipped with fine-grained defect metadata (e.g., description, type, severity) alongside dynamic state annotations, capturing the complete evolutionary trajectory of a defect throughout the multi-round process. We obtain several findings through extensive experiments on MCR-Bench with mainstream LLMs. (1) Limited overall capability: experiments reveal that mainstream LLMs exhibit limited overall performance in defect detection and defect lifecycle state tracking, with performance degrading significantly as the number of interaction rounds increases; (2) Defect-sensitive performance: LLMs' performance varies substantially across different defect types and severity levels, with semantically complex or low-salience defects being significantly more likely to be missed; (3) Underlying Failure Mechanisms: our in-depth error analysis dissects the distinct drivers of false positives and false negatives, revealing critical weaknesses such as cross-round temporal misalignment and inadequate long-range memory.
summaryZh: MCR-Bench 是首个专门针对真实世界多轮代码审查场景设计的缺陷状态感知基准。该基准包含 2,269 个多轮代码审查任务，涵盖五种主流编程语言，并为每个任务提供了细粒度的缺陷元数据和动态状态标注。研究通过对主流大模型进行实验发现，模型在处理多轮交互时的缺陷检测能力会随轮次增加而显著下降，且对语义复杂或低显著性的缺陷表现较差。该工作揭示了当前大模型在代码审查任务中的局限性，并深入分析了导致假阳性和假阴性的底层机制，为提升模型在软件工程中的实际应用能力提供了重要参考。

指基准测试能够识别并追踪缺陷在多轮审查过程中的演变状态。
指代码审查中开发者与审查者之间多次往复的沟通与修改过程。
